The House passed its version of the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act on Wednesday in a 216-212 vote, including a provision to extend the 2015 Cybersecurity and Information Sharing Act for another decade. The $1.15 trillion Pentagon policy roadmap received support from only a handful of Democrats and placed no curbs on President Donald Trump’s use of U.S. military forces, including in relation to the Iran war. The included Widespread Information Management for the Welfare of Infrastructure and Government Act would reauthorize CISA 2015, which provides legal protections for private-sector and federal sharing of data on criminal and nation-state hacking threats.

The statute briefly expired last year, leaving federal officials in the dark about the full scope of digital threats to U.S. critical infrastructure, before it was temporarily extended through September 30. The WIMWIG Act was approved by the House Homeland Security Committee last year but has not received a floor vote and faces opposition in the Senate. Sen. Rand Paul has vowed to block any reauthorization unless it includes language barring the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency from work to counter online disinformation, even though the article notes the law and the agency are not directly linked.

The Senate’s draft of the NDAA does not include a matching extension, though the issue is expected to come up during the amendment process. The bill has also hit a roadblock with Democrats, who earlier this month tanked consideration of the legislation in their fight to rein in Trump on Iran. Separately, the House bill does not include the Senate’s proposal to merge two major Pentagon cyber roles, but it does call for a “review and realignment” of all Pentagon cyber roles.

  • The House is using the defense policy bill as the vehicle to renew CISA 2015 even though the standalone WIMWIG Act previously cleared the House Homeland Security Committee but has not received a floor vote.
  • A major obstacle to reauthorization is not the information-sharing law itself, but Sen. Rand Paul’s demand for limits on CISA’s work related to online disinformation, despite the article noting that the law and the agency are not directly linked.
  • The House and Senate cyber provisions diverge beyond CISA 2015, with the Senate proposing to merge two Pentagon cyber leadership roles while the House instead calls for a broader review and realignment of Pentagon cyber roles.
  • The temporary extension of CISA 2015 expires on September 30, but the article describes multiple unresolved legislative hurdles, including Senate opposition, an amendment process, and eventual House-Senate negotiations.

A fake Ingersoll Rand lookalike domain registered just eight days earlier passed SPF, DKIM, and Microsoft’s DMARC best-guess because the attacker controlled the domain and sent through Amazon SES. The key takeaway is that email authentication cannot prove trustworthiness; detecting this kind of BEC requires behavioral signals like domain age, remittance-change language, and out-of-band payment verification.

An accounts-payable-adjacent mailbox at a commercial mechanical contractor received a payment-status request that appeared to come from Ingersoll Rand. The message used the lookalike domain ingersollrandcompany[.]com, while the real Ingersoll Rand domain is ingersollrand.com. The lookalike domain had been registered eight days before the email was sent, had redacted registrant details behind Cloudflare, had no public A record, and appeared to exist only to send mail.

The email passed SPF, passed DKIM, and received Microsoft’s dmarc=bestguesspass, but the article says these results did not prove the sender was trustworthy. SPF passed because the attacker controlled the lookalike domain and authorized Amazon SES, while DKIM passed with header.d=amazonses.com. The lookalike domain published no DMARC record, and Microsoft applied a best-guess heuristic rather than enforcing a published DMARC policy.

The message asked about payment status and directed replies to its_remittance@ingersollrandcompany[.]com, making it a remittance diversion attempt tied to a bank detail change. The article says authentication was not what stopped the message; Microsoft categorized it as PHISH with a spam confidence level of 5, and Themis scored it 78 percent as invoice phishing. The detection was driven by the payment-request language, the newly registered return-path domain, and community resolution of similar incidents.

  • DMARC on a legitimate company’s real domain does not protect against fraud sent from a separate lookalike domain, even when that lookalike closely resembles the trusted brand.
  • A newly registered domain used only for email is a stronger warning sign in this case than SPF, DKIM, or DMARC results, especially when paired with a payment or remittance request.
  • Legitimate services such as Amazon SES, Microsoft SafeLinks, and tracking redirects can appear in the delivery path of a fraudulent email, so their presence should not be treated as proof that the message is safe.

In plain words

A new research paper tested five major AI coding models and found they still sometimes make up software package names that do not exist on PyPI or npm, two places developers get code libraries. Researchers found 53 made-up names that were still available to register, and every tested model had suggested those names. This matters because a criminal could register one of those names with harmful code, and a developer using AI-generated code might be tricked into adding it to a real project. The study did not find that this has already happened with those names, but it shows why developers need to check new AI-suggested dependencies before trusting them.

Summary
A new preprint found that five frontier LLMs still hallucinate nonexistent PyPI and npm package names at similar rates, creating 53 currently registrable slopsquatting targets shared across all tested models. The key risk is that attackers could register these invented names and wait for AI coding tools to recommend malicious dependencies to developers.

A new independent research preprint examining nearly 200,000 code-generation responses found that five frontier large language models continue to invent package names that do not exist on PyPI or npm. The tested models were Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and DeepSeek V3.2. Their overall package-hallucination rates ranged from 4.62% to 6.10%, a much narrower spread than earlier research but not an elimination of the problem.

The study initially found 127 package names generated by every model in the test group. After review by PyPI Security and Socket, researchers determined that 53 of those names, 41 on PyPI and 12 on npm, were still available for registration as of April 2026. The article explains that an attacker could publish malware under one of these names and wait for an AI coding tool to recommend it to a developer, a technique known as slopsquatting.

Socket’s review also showed that registry lookups alone can misclassify valid imports as hallucinations, because some framework-provided modules do not exist as standalone registry packages. Four high-volume npm entries were valid Ember.js imports resolved through ember-source, while other names were removed because they already existed or were under a security hold. The study identified potential targets rather than an active attack, and it found no evidence that any of the 53 names had been registered maliciously or used to compromise developers.

  • The gap between the best and worst model hallucination rates narrowed sharply to 1.48 percentage points, but none of the five newer models beat the earlier study’s lowest individual result of about 3.6% for GPT-4 Turbo.
  • A package name can be a higher-value slopsquatting target when it is hallucinated by multiple model providers, because one malicious registration could potentially appear in suggestions from several AI coding tools.
  • Registry lookup results alone can overstate package hallucinations because valid framework-provided imports, such as Ember.js modules resolved through ember-source, may not exist as standalone registry packages.
  • GPT-5.4-mini’s measured hallucination rate is harder to compare directly with the other models because it refused 32.14% of prompts and its rate was calculated only from compliant, parseable responses.
  • Lockfiles and version pinning do not address the initial risk of accepting an unfamiliar AI-suggested dependency, so the first introduction of a new package still requires review of its name, publisher, history, and relationship to the intended project.
Key Points
  • 01A new independent research preprint found that Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and DeepSeek V3.2 still invent nonexistent package names on PyPI and npm.
  • 02The five tested models had overall package-hallucination rates ranging from 4.62% to 6.10% across 199,845 responses generated between April 22 and April 28, 2026.
  • 03Researchers initially found 127 package names generated by all five models, and reviews by PyPI Security and Socket determined that 53 of those names were still available for registration as of April 2026.
  • 04Socket’s review removed six npm candidates from the exploitable set, including four valid Ember.js imports and two names that were already an existing package or security-hold package.
  • 05The study identified potential slopsquatting targets, but it found no evidence that any of the 53 names had been registered maliciously or used to compromise developers.

The article explains how ransomware has evolved from classic ransomware, where attackers encrypt an organization’s data and demand payment, into modern ransomware, also called double extortion ransomware. In classic ransomware, the main decision for leaders is often whether recovery costs more than paying the ransom. Reliable, secured, and separated backups can reduce the impact by allowing an organization to restore data without paying.

Modern ransomware adds a major change: attackers steal copies of data before encrypting systems and then demand payment to decrypt data and prevent the release of sensitive information. The article says these attacks are more complex because attackers may wait inside a network, move laterally, access additional resources, and create new ways to steal data. This changes the response from a recovery problem into a broader risk management problem.

The article uses the NIST incident response lifecycle to compare how organizations should respond to classic and modern ransomware. For modern ransomware, incident responders must quickly determine what data was encrypted, what data was accessed or stolen, how it was stolen, and whether attackers still have access. Executives must also consider notification requirements, regulation, reputation, public relations, and whether paying the ransom addresses the risks created by stolen data.

  • The article highlights forensic data backups as a readiness measure because they can radically improve investigators’ ability to understand what happened during a future attack.

The people affected are Google Workspace users and organizations whose documents may contain sensitive information. The broader risk is that important files could leave the organization without being noticed unless investigators understand what the records do and do not show.

Summary
Google Workspace audit logs can support Google Drive data-exfiltration threat hunting, but investigators must account for missing fields like user agents and paths, event-chain complexity, and third-party app activity. The key practical takeaway is to reconstruct file context from logs and analyze download, sharing, and permission-change events to distinguish suspicious mass access from benign activity.

The article explains how to threat hunt in Google Workspace, with a primary focus on possible data exfiltration from Google Drive. It looks for activities that may indicate data leaving the environment, such as massive file downloads, file sharing, third-party application activity, previews, prints, views, and files emailed as attachments. The authors emphasize that Google Workspace is widely used by organizations and individuals, making it important to understand how its logs can be used during investigations.

A major challenge described in the article is that Google Workspace logs lack several useful forensic details, including user agent information, file paths, and log entries for anonymous access to publicly shared files. The authors recommend restructuring event parameters, splitting chains of events into separate records, and creating a unique event ID from id.uniqueQualifier, id.time, and the event position in the original array. They also highlight the originating_app_id field because third-party applications can perform actions on behalf of users and make IP-based investigation results appear inconsistent.

The article details how sharing and permission changes appear in the logs, including visibility changes, access scope changes, and differences between file-level and folder-level permission changes. It also describes a case where 15,000 files were downloaded in a short time, initially appearing suspicious, but further analysis showed the files came from a personal backup folder uploaded by the organizational user. To determine file locations, the authors reconstructed paths from add_to_folder events using document and destination folder identifiers, noting that this log-based approach can help investigate past states while the Google Workspace API shows only current status.

  • Anonymous access to a file shared publicly through “people_with_link” permissions does not create a log entry, leaving a visibility gap for investigators.
  • Filtering out events that include originating_app_id can reduce false IP-location anomalies because third-party applications may perform actions from hosting provider addresses rather than the user’s actual location.
  • Google Workspace logs record link-sharing permission changes in two stages, first changing visibility and access scope to private or none and then changing them to the requested shared state.
  • When a folder’s permissions are changed, Google Workspace logs one user-driven change_user_access event for the folder and then SYSTEM-driven change_user_access_hierarchy_reconciled events for each contained file or subfolder.
  • Reconstructing file paths from historical add_to_folder log events can be more accurate for past investigations than querying the Google Drive API, because the API only reflects the file’s current location.
Key Points
  • 01Google Workspace audit logs lack several useful forensic fields, including user agent, file paths, and log entries for anonymous access to publicly shared files.
  • 02The article recommends restructuring Google Workspace event parameters and splitting chains of events into separate records to make the logs easier to investigate.
  • 03The originating_app_id field can identify third-party applications that performed actions on behalf of users, which helped explain suspicious-looking IP geolocation anomalies caused by applications such as Slack using hosting provider addresses.
  • 04Potential Google Drive data exfiltration can be hunted through events such as download, email_as_attachment, preview, print, and view, as well as through sharing and permission-change events.
  • 05The authors reconstructed file paths from add_to_folder events by using doc_id, doc_title, destination_folder_id, and destination_folder_title, which helped determine that a mass download of 15,000 files came from a personal backup folder and was not malicious.

The article describes three ways upgrade-based remediation can fail. Some packages, such as the deprecated Node HTTP client request, have no fixed version and would require migration to alternatives such as axios or node-fetch. It argues that large CVE backlogs are becoming more urgent because AI can help find vulnerabilities faster and combine medium-severity issues into more serious exploit patterns. The piece contrasts the promise of agents that triage, investigate, decide, and remediate with the risk of deploying that level of autonomy too early.

A central distinction is between an agent that recommends and an agent that acts. The article says a bad recommendation may cost a few minutes of analyst review, while a bad automated remediation could revoke a credential, quarantine a production workload, lock an account, and damage business trust in the security team. The author recommends separating agent work into detection, enrichment, correlation, recommendation, and action, then granting trust to each stage independently.

The article also says AI agents should be instrumented like employees on probation, with every decision logged, attributable, and reconstructable after the fact. Mitiga’s premiere episode of Mitiga Mic features co-founder and CTO Ofer Maor discussing the company’s origin and its evolution from cloud incident response services into a platform for cloud, SaaS, and identity detection and response. Maor says Mitiga was created because traditional incident response often depends on teams waiting for data and permissions, while cloud environments require a different approach. He explains that the company began by providing services and used that real-world breach experience to guide the platform it later built.

A major theme of the interview is that cloud investigations depend on telemetry because responders cannot image cloud provider hardware the way they could with on-premises systems. Maor says cloud telemetry is not always enabled by default, has poor retention, and can be too large and costly for traditional SIEM-style collection. Mitiga therefore built its own forensic data lake, along with data normalization, enrichment, and automation capabilities for investigation and detection.

The discussion also covers Mitiga’s expansion beyond public cloud platforms into identity and SaaS because attackers move across systems through federated identity and single sign-on. Maor describes how Mitiga added detection capabilities, mapped alerts to identities and entities, and built AI features to reduce triage time for analysts. He says Mitiga’s AI work is based on observing its own investigation team and automating steps that analysts already perform in the platform.

  • Mitiga’s service-first approach gave the company direct exposure to real cloud breaches, which Ofer Maor says shaped what the platform needed to automate and support.
  • In one breach example, having the right data allowed investigators to challenge an attacker’s claims about stolen data within hours and helped reduce a ransom payment from millions to $250,000.
  • Maor argues that cloud detection became easier for Mitiga only after it had already built data collection, normalization, enrichment, and investigation automation.
  • Mitiga’s AI work is described as emerging from watching its own investigation team use the platform daily, rather than from a separate effort to add AI for its own sake.
  • Maor says AI-driven triage is intended to reduce analyst work from hours to minutes or even seconds by presenting an assessment when an alert is opened.
Key Points
  • 01Mitiga was founded to rethink incident response for cloud environments because traditional response teams often wait on data, permissions, and access that may not exist in modern cloud systems.
  • 02Ofer Maor said cloud investigations depend entirely on telemetry because organizations do not own the underlying machines or data center rooms, and many cloud logs are not enabled by default or retained for long.
  • 03Mitiga built its own data lake after finding that Splunk was not suited to the scale and cost profile of broad cloud telemetry collection.
  • 04The company expanded beyond public cloud platforms into SaaS and identity because attackers move wherever federated identity and single sign-on access allow them to go.
  • 05Mitiga added detection and AI-driven triage capabilities on top of its collected data to help analysts investigate alerts faster and address gaps in cloud security skills and staffing.

Lateral movement is moving from one connected system to another after gaining access somewhere.
also: move laterally
Lateral movement path technique
A lateral movement path is a route an attacker can take to move from one system or account to another.
lateral-movement capability technique
Lateral-movement capability is the ability for an attacker to move from one compromised system to others inside the same network.
law enforcement organization
Law enforcement means police or government agencies responsible for investigating and stopping crime.
Leaked credentials concept
Leaked credentials are usernames, passwords, or login tokens that have been exposed to people who should not have them.
lease-to-own agreements concept
Lease-to-own agreements let customers rent an item with the option or plan to own it after payments are completed.
least privilege concept
A security principle that gives users and programs only the minimum level of access they need to do their job, nothing more.
least-privilege access concept
Least-privilege access means giving people only the minimum access they need to do their work.
Least-privilege tokens concept
Least-privilege tokens are access tokens limited to only the permissions needed for a specific task.
ledger concept
A ledger is a record of transactions or changes, often used to track money, access, or system activity.
Legacy Medical IoT product
Legacy Medical IoT refers to older internet-connected medical devices that may be harder to secure or update.
legacy systems concept
Legacy systems are older computer systems or software that are still in use, often because replacing them is difficult or expensive.
Legal protections concept
Legal protections are laws or agreements that shield people or organizations from certain liabilities or penalties.
Legitimate credentials concept
Legitimate credentials are real usernames, passwords, tokens, or keys that attackers may steal and use to look like valid users.
Legitimate services concept
Legitimate services are real, trusted online platforms or tools that attackers may abuse to hide malicious activity.
lethal trifecta concept
The lethal trifecta is a security risk pattern where an AI agent has private data access, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to send data out.
lg.svg other
lg.svg is a named SVG image file that could be referenced as part of a website, message, or investigation artifact.
Linux product
Linux is an operating system commonly used on servers and developer machines.
Linux distributions product
Linux distributions are packaged versions of the Linux operating system that include the kernel, tools, and software.
Linux namespaces concept
Linux namespaces are operating-system features that isolate processes, networks, and filesystems, often used by containers.
Linux scanning and exploitation payload tool
A Linux scanning and exploitation payload is malicious or testing code that searches Linux systems for weaknesses and tries to exploit them.
also: Linux payload, Linux executables, executable
living-off-the-land technique
Living-off-the-land is when attackers use built-in system tools instead of obvious malware to hide their activity.
LLMs concept
LLMs are large language models, which are AI systems trained on lots of text so they can generate and understand language.
local privilege escalation technique
A technique where an attacker with limited system access exploits a flaw to gain higher administrative rights.
LockBit 3.0 malware
LockBit 3.0 is a major ransomware variant used by the LockBit cybercriminal operation.
Lockfiles concept
Lockfiles record the exact versions of software dependencies a project uses so builds are more predictable.
Lodash product
Lodash is a popular JavaScript utility library used by developers to simplify common programming tasks.
logging concept
Logging is the recording of events and actions so people can review what happened later.
login activity concept
Records of user sign-in attempts, often monitored for anomalies like unusual locations or failure spikes.
login credentials concept
Information like usernames and passwords used to access accounts.
Logistics systems concept
Logistics systems are software and processes used to manage shipping, warehousing, inventory movement, and supply chains.
London Metropolitan Police’s Cyber Crime Unit organization
London Metropolitan Police’s Cyber Crime Unit is a police team in London that investigates cybercrime.
Lookalike domain technique
A lookalike domain is a web address designed to resemble a trusted domain and trick users.
also: lookalike-domain fraud
Los Angeles transit agency organization
A Los Angeles transit agency is a public transportation organization serving the Los Angeles area and may operate systems that need cybersecurity protection.
Low-complexity attacks concept
Low-complexity attacks are attacks that are relatively easy to carry out because they require few special conditions or skills.
LSASS concept
A critical Windows process that handles user logins and authentication, frequently targeted by attackers to steal password hashes.
lure technique
A lure is bait used by attackers, such as a fake offer or message, to persuade someone to click or act.
lures technique
Lures are messages, files, or themes attackers use to tempt people into clicking a link, opening an attachment, or taking another risky action.
machine learning concept
Machine learning is a type of AI where computers learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions.
macOS product
Apple's desktop operating system for Mac computers.
MagicalPuff96 threat-actor
MagicalPuff96 is an online alias referenced in security reporting.
mail server tool
A mail server is a computer system that sends, receives, and stores email for users or organizations.
Mainstream support concept
Mainstream support is the normal support period when a vendor still provides regular updates, fixes, and feature improvements for a product.
Maintainers concept
Maintainers are the people responsible for updating, reviewing, and managing a software project.
also: maintainer
Malicious concept
Malicious means intentionally harmful, such as software or behavior designed to damage, steal, or deceive.
malicious activity concept
Malicious activity is any harmful or unauthorized action, such as stealing data, spreading malware, or breaking into systems.
malicious actors threat-actor
Malicious actors are people or groups who intentionally try to harm systems, steal data, or commit cybercrime.
Malicious cyber actors threat-actor
Malicious cyber actors are people or groups that use computers and networks to cause harm, steal data, or break into systems.
Malicious dataset technique
A malicious dataset is a data collection designed to trick software or AI systems into running harmful actions when it is opened or processed.
Malicious File concept
A malicious file is a file designed to harm a computer, steal information, or help an attacker gain access.
malicious page concept
A malicious page is a web page designed to trick users, steal information, or attack their device.
malicious project file interactions technique
Malicious project file interactions are attacks where opening or processing a project file triggers harmful behavior.
malicious software concept
Malicious software is software designed to harm systems, steal information, or give attackers control.
malicious workflows technique
Malicious workflows are automation scripts, such as CI/CD jobs, that have been created or changed to do harmful actions.
Maliciously crafted URL technique
A maliciously crafted URL is a web link deliberately designed to trigger a bug, steal data, or trick a user.
malware concept
Malware is software made to harm, spy on, or take control of computers or data.
malware delivery technique
Malware delivery is the process attackers use to get malicious software onto a victim's device.
malware-based detection technique
Malware-based detection identifies threats by looking for known malicious files, code patterns, or malware behavior.
Managed CDR product
Managed CDR is a managed cybersecurity service or content disarm and reconstruction offering referenced in security reporting.
managed identities concept
Managed identities are cloud-provided identities that let applications access resources without storing passwords or secret keys in code.
Manifold Security organization
Manifold Security is a cybersecurity company or research organization name referenced in security reporting.
also: Manifold
manipulation of data technique
Manipulation of data means changing, deleting, or falsifying information, often to mislead people or disrupt systems.
manufacturing plants concept
Manufacturing plants are facilities where goods are produced, and they can be cybersecurity targets because they rely on connected industrial systems.
Markdown product
A lightweight text formatting syntax that's popular for documentation, also used in phishing kits and malware notes.
masquerading
Masquerading is when attackers disguise malicious files, processes, or accounts to look legitimate.
Mass assignment vulnerability
Mass assignment is a software flaw where an app accidentally lets users change fields they should not control.
Massive organization
Massive is a named entity referenced in security reporting, likely a tool, service, or organization name.
Mastercard organization
Mastercard is a global payment card network used for credit, debit, and digital payments.
MaxMind organization
MaxMind is a company known for IP geolocation and fraud-detection data services.
McKinsey organization
McKinsey is a global management consulting firm.
McKinsey's State of AI report product
McKinsey's State of AI report is a research report from McKinsey about how organizations are adopting and using artificial intelligence.
MCP protocol
MCP, or Model Context Protocol, is a standard way for AI assistants to connect to external tools, files, and services.
MCP Server tool
An MCP Server is a server that implements the Model Context Protocol to connect AI systems with tools, data, or services.
Medical Devices product
Medical devices are healthcare instruments or machines, such as monitors or scanners, that may also contain software and network connections.
meeting summarizers tool
Meeting summarizers are tools that use software, often AI, to create notes or summaries from meetings.
Megalodon malware
Megalodon is a named malware family, tool, or campaign referenced in security reporting.
Megalodon campaign threat-actor
Megalodon campaign is a named cyberattack campaign referenced in security reporting.
Metadata concept
Metadata is data that describes other data, such as when a file was created, who sent an email, or where a photo was taken.
Metropolitan Police organization
The Metropolitan Police is the police service responsible for Greater London, commonly known as the Met Police.
MFA concept
MFA is the shortened name for multi-factor authentication, a login process that uses more than one proof of identity.
MGM organization
MGM is a hospitality and entertainment company that has been referenced in major cyberattack reporting.
microsoft organization
Microsoft is a major technology company that makes Windows, Office, Azure, and many enterprise security products.
Microsoft accounts product
Microsoft accounts are user accounts used to sign in to Microsoft services such as Outlook, Windows, Xbox, and Azure-related tools.
Microsoft Defender product
Microsoft Defender is Microsoft’s built-in security software for detecting and blocking malware and other threats.
Microsoft Exchange Server product
Microsoft Exchange Server is Microsoft’s email and calendar server software used by organizations.
Microsoft SafeLinks product
Microsoft SafeLinks is a Microsoft security feature that checks links in emails and documents to help block malicious websites.
also: SafeLinks
Microsoft Threat Intelligence organization
Microsoft Threat Intelligence is Microsoft’s security research and reporting group that tracks cyber threats.
Microsoft's DMARC best-guess technique
Microsoft's DMARC best-guess is a Microsoft email-security behavior that estimates how to handle a message when DMARC authentication information is incomplete or ambiguous.
also: best-guess heuristic, bestguesspass
microsoft-365
Microsoft 365 is Microsoft’s cloud productivity and security suite including Office apps, email, storage, and collaboration tools.
microsoft-authenticator
Microsoft Authenticator is a mobile app for multi-factor authentication and passwordless sign-ins.
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listKeys/action concept
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listKeys/action is an Azure permission that allows listing storage account keys.
Mimikatz tool
Mimikatz is a well-known security tool often used by attackers and defenders to extract passwords and authentication tokens from Windows systems.
Ministry of Foreign Affairs organization
A Ministry of Foreign Affairs is a government department that manages a country's diplomacy and relations with other countries.
misconfiguration vulnerability
Misconfiguration is an unsafe or incorrect setting that can expose a system to attack.
Misconfigurations vulnerability
Misconfigurations are incorrect settings that can accidentally expose systems or make attacks easier.
Misconfigured or abandoned agent concept
A misconfigured or abandoned agent is management software left insecure or unused in a way attackers may abuse.
misuse concept
Misuse is using a system, account, or feature in a harmful or unauthorized way.
mitiga
Mitiga is a cloud incident response and threat detection company.
Mitiga CDR product
Mitiga CDR is a cloud detection and response security product or service from Mitiga.
Mitiga Mic product
Mitiga Mic is a named product or tool referenced in cloud security reporting.
mitigation and remediation measures concept
Mitigation and remediation measures are steps taken to reduce a security risk and fix the underlying problem.
MITRE organization
MITRE is a nonprofit organization known in cybersecurity for maintaining public knowledge bases like ATT&CK and CVE-related resources.
MITRE ATLAS tool
MITRE ATLAS is a knowledge base that describes attacks and risks involving artificial intelligence systems.
MITRE ATT&CK tool
MITRE ATT&CK is a framework for naming and organizing attacker techniques.
also: ATT&CK
MITRE ATT&CK concept
MITRE ATT&CK is a public knowledge base that organizes common attacker tactics and techniques so defenders can describe and compare threats consistently.
MITRE ATT&CK T1562 technique
MITRE ATT&CK T1562 is the catalog entry for techniques attackers use to impair or disable security defenses.
mobile app product
A mobile app is software designed to run on a smartphone or tablet.
Mobile application product
A mobile application is software that runs on a phone or tablet.
mobile pay numbers concept
Mobile pay numbers are payment identifiers linked to a phone-based payment method or mobile wallet.
mobile phone numbers concept
Mobile phone numbers are personal contact numbers that can be sensitive because attackers may use them for scams or account takeover attempts.
Model update concept
A model update is a change to an AI model that can alter how it behaves, responds, or performs.
also: model updates
Models concept
Models are AI or machine-learning systems trained to make predictions, generate content, or process information.
also: models, datasets, and solutions
Modern ransomware malware
Modern ransomware often combines file encryption with data theft and threats to leak stolen information.
Monday.com product
Monday.com is a cloud-based work management and collaboration platform.
Monthly Cyber Threat Level concept
Monthly Cyber Threat Level is a recurring rating or report that summarizes how serious current cyber risks are.
mpsvc.dll tool
mpsvc.dll is a Windows system library associated with firewall or security services.
MSPs organization
MSPs are managed service providers that remotely manage IT systems for customer organizations.
Multi-cloud organizations concept
Multi-cloud organizations use cloud services from more than one provider, such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
multi-factor authentication concept
Multi-factor authentication is a login method that asks users to prove who they are in more than one way.
multi-layered network detections technique
Multi-layered network detections use several kinds of network signals and rules together to spot suspicious activity.

Multi-turn manipulation is an attack that influences an AI system over several back-and-forth messages instead of a single prompt.
multifactor authentication technique
Multifactor authentication requires more than one proof of identity to log in, such as a password plus another verification method.
mutation engine technique
A mutation engine is code that changes malware’s appearance so it is harder for security tools to recognize.
Nati Tal other
Nati Tal is an individual referenced in security reporting, likely as a researcher, executive, or source.
also: principal researcher
nation-state concept
A nation-state is a country acting through its government, often used in cybersecurity to describe government-backed hacking activity.
National Defense Authorization Act concept
The National Defense Authorization Act is a yearly U.S. law that sets defense priorities and funding, often including cybersecurity provisions.
National Diplomatic Academy organization
A National Diplomatic Academy is an institution that trains diplomats and foreign-affairs officials.
National Diplomatic Academy Online Education System product
The National Diplomatic Academy Online Education System is an online education platform associated with diplomatic training.
National Security Agency organization
The National Security Agency is a U.S. government agency focused on signals intelligence and cybersecurity.
Nearest-neighbor attack technique
A nearest-neighbor attack is an attack that abuses systems that find similar items, such as embeddings or recommendations, to cause wrong matches or leaks.
Nemesis Market organization
Nemesis Market was a dark web marketplace where illegal goods or services were reportedly bought and sold.
NetFlow protocol
NetFlow is a network protocol and data format that summarizes traffic flows between systems for monitoring and analysis.
netskope organization
Netskope is a cybersecurity company that provides cloud security, secure web access, and zero-trust networking products.
Netskope One product
Netskope One is a Netskope platform for security and networking functions.
Netskope One AI Red Teaming product
Netskope One AI Red Teaming is a Netskope product or service for testing AI systems against security risks.
also: AI Red Teaming
Netskope One AI Security product
Netskope One AI Security is a Netskope product or service for helping organizations monitor and control security risks from AI use.
netskope-one-ai-guardrails
Netskope One AI Guardrails is a security product designed to help organizations control and protect use of AI tools.
Network Access concept
Network access means the ability to connect to and use a computer network or resources on it.
network architecture concept
Network architecture is the design of how computers, servers, cloud services, and security controls connect and communicate.
network data concept
Network data is information about communications between computers, such as addresses, ports, traffic volume, and sometimes packet contents.
Network detection and response concept
Network detection and response monitors network traffic to find and help respond to suspicious or malicious behavior.
network traffic concept
Network traffic is the data moving between computers, servers, phones, and other devices over a network.
network visibility concept
Network visibility is the ability to see and understand traffic, devices, and activity on a network.
new-york
New York is a U.S. state often mentioned in cybersecurity stories involving companies, victims, laws, or courts.
NewEdge Government platform product
NewEdge Government platform is a named government-focused technology platform referenced in security reporting.
newly registered domain concept
A newly registered domain is an internet domain name that was recently created and may be suspicious in some threat investigations.
Newtonsoft.Json tool
Newtonsoft.Json is a popular .NET library used to read and write JSON data.
Newtonsoftt.Json.Net product
Newtonsoftt.Json.Net is a suspicious or lookalike package name that resembles the legitimate Newtonsoft.Json library.
Nextcloud proxy path concept
A Nextcloud proxy path is a URL route used through a proxy to reach a Nextcloud file-sharing or collaboration service.
nghttp2 tool
nghttp2 is an open-source implementation of the HTTP/2 protocol used by many software projects.

Nichirei is a Japanese company known for food and logistics businesses.
Nichirei Logistics Group organization
Nichirei Logistics Group is a logistics and cold-storage company based in Japan.
Nidec organization
Nidec is a Japanese manufacturer of electric motors and related components.
Ninja Cable tool
Ninja Cable is a hardware security tool or malicious cable referenced in security reporting.
NIST organization
NIST is the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which creates widely used security standards and guidance.
NIST AI Risk Management Framework concept
The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is U.S. guidance for identifying and managing risks from artificial intelligence systems.
NIST incident response lifecycle concept
The NIST incident response lifecycle is a model for preparing for, detecting, containing, recovering from, and learning after incidents.
NIST SP 800-61 other
NIST SP 800-61 is a U.S. government guide for computer security incident handling.
Node product
Node usually refers to Node.js, a runtime that lets JavaScript run outside a web browser.
Node group concept
A node group is a set of worker machines in a Kubernetes cluster, often managed together.
node-fetch tool

Node.js product
Node.js is a JavaScript runtime used to build server-side and command-line applications.
Node.js product
Node.js is a platform that lets developers run JavaScript code outside a web browser, often on servers.

NodeBB is an open-source web forum platform built with Node.js.
Non-sensitive concept
Non-sensitive information is data that is not considered private, confidential, or especially harmful if shared.
non-sensitive customer information concept
Non-sensitive customer information is customer data considered less private or risky than items like passwords, payment details, or government IDs.
North America other
North America is a geographic region including countries such as the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
north-korea other
North Korea is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reports because some hacking groups are alleged to operate on its behalf.

Novel malware is malicious software that is new or not yet widely recognized by security tools.
npm product

npm audit tool
npm audit is a command that checks Node.js project dependencies for known security vulnerabilities.
npm package concept
An npm package is a reusable JavaScript software bundle that developers can install from the npm ecosystem.
npm packages product
npm packages are reusable JavaScript software modules distributed through the npm package ecosystem.

nuget

NVIDIA organization
NVIDIA is a technology company known for graphics chips, AI hardware, and related software.

OAuth token hygiene means safely issuing, storing, limiting, monitoring, and revoking OAuth access tokens.
obfuscation technique
The technique of making code or data deliberately hard to understand to avoid detection by security tools.
Office 365 product
Office 365 is Microsoft’s cloud-based email, office apps, and collaboration service, now commonly called Microsoft 365.
official job titles concept
Official job titles are formal names for roles in an organization and can reveal information useful for targeting or impersonation.

OIDC stands for OpenID Connect, a protocol that helps apps confirm a user's identity during sign-in.
Okta organization

OMB organization
OMB is the U.S. Office of Management and Budget, which helps set federal policy including technology and security guidance.
OMB M-24-10 concept
OMB M-24-10 is a U.S. Office of Management and Budget memorandum about federal governance and risk management for artificial intelligence.

on-premises concept
On-premises means software or hardware runs in an organization’s own facilities instead of in the cloud.
online disinformation concept
Online disinformation is false or misleading information spread on the internet on purpose.
online education system product
An online education system is a website or platform used to deliver classes, assignments, and school services over the internet.
Online Killers Marketplace organization
Online Killers Marketplace is a named online marketplace referenced in reporting about alleged harm-for-hire activity.
online marketplaces concept
Online marketplaces are websites or platforms where buyers and sellers trade goods, services, or digital items.
online services concept
Online services are websites, apps, or internet-based systems that provide functions to users over the internet.
OnlyOffice product

open internet access concept
Open internet access means a system or user can connect broadly to websites and online services without tight restrictions.
open source concept
Open source means software whose source code is publicly available for people to inspect, use, modify, and share.
open source packages product

openai organization

also: AI company, company
OpenAI's research environment organization
OpenAI's research environment is the internal or controlled computing setup used by OpenAI for AI research and testing.
also: our research testing environment

OpenID Connect is an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 that lets apps verify who a user is.
Operational technology concept
Operational technology is hardware and software used to monitor or control physical equipment, such as factory machines, power systems, or industrial sensors.
operator panel tool
An operator panel is a control interface used by administrators or attackers to manage a system, tool, or campaign.
operators concept
Operators are the people or groups running a system, service, campaign, or criminal operation.
Opportunistic attackers threat-actor
Opportunistic attackers look for easy targets rather than focusing on one specific victim.
option element protocol
An option element is an HTML item that represents a selectable choice inside controls like drop-down menus.
oracle
Oracle is a technology company known for databases, enterprise software, cloud services, and Java-related products.
Oracle WebLogic Server product
Oracle WebLogic Server is an Oracle product used to run and manage Java-based web applications for businesses.
Organization restriction headers concept
Organization restriction headers are request headers used to limit access to resources based on an allowed organization.
organization settings concept
Organization settings are configuration pages for managing an organization’s members, rules, and preferences.
originating_app_id concept
originating_app_id is a field name that identifies which application originated an event or request.

OSINT, or open-source intelligence, is information gathered from publicly available sources such as websites, social media, and records.
OT concept

Outdated means software, data, or settings are old and may be missing important fixes or protections.
overseas diplomats organization

oversight concept
Oversight means watching over an activity or organization to make sure rules are followed and problems are caught.

OWASP Top 10 concept
OWASP Top 10 is a widely used list of the most important web application security risks.
OWASP Top 10 for LLMs concept
The OWASP Top 10 for LLMs is a list of major security risks for applications that use large language models.
PaaS concept
A cloud computing model where a provider offers a platform allowing customers to develop, run, and manage applications without maintaining infrastructure.

also: package-hallucination rates, package hallucination
package metadata concept
Package metadata is the basic information about a software package, such as its name, version, author, and dependencies.
package registries concept
Package registries are online repositories where developers publish and download reusable software libraries.
package registry cache proxy tool
A package registry cache proxy is a server that stores and forwards software package downloads so teams can control, speed up, or inspect what developers install.
package versions concept
Package versions are numbered releases of software components that help track updates and fixes.

packages.lock.json is a software dependency lock file that records exact package versions used by a project.

Packagist is the main public package repository used by Composer for PHP software libraries.
packet capture technique
Packet capture is the recording of network traffic so it can be inspected and analyzed.
Parliament organization
Parliament is the legislative body that the article says the Information Commissioner is directly accountable to.

Password health describes whether passwords are strong, unique, and not known to be stolen.
password managers tool
Password managers are apps that store and fill in passwords so users can use strong, unique passwords for different accounts.
password reset concept
The process of changing a user's password, typically after they've forgotten it or it's been compromised.
password resets concept
The process of changing or recovering a password, often used when a user forgets their current password.
passwords concept
Passwords are secret words or strings used to prove you are allowed to access an account or device.
PAT-based server concept
A PAT-based server is a server that authenticates using personal access tokens instead of, or in addition to, other login methods.
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.

patient data concept
Sensitive health information about individuals, protected by laws like HIPAA, and a high-value target for ransomware and data breaches.
patient-safety concept
Patient safety is the prevention of harm to people receiving medical care.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
payload execution technique
Payload execution means running the main malicious code or action after an attacker has gained a way into a system.
Payload Execution by Web Server technique
Payload Execution by Web Server means a web server is being used to run code or commands that an attacker supplied.
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
payment card details concept
Credit or debit card information such as the number, expiration date, and CVV, highly sought by criminals for fraud.
payment information concept
Payment information is data used to make purchases, such as card numbers, billing details, or payment account identifiers.
payment methods concept
Payment methods are ways people pay for goods or services, such as cards, bank transfers, or cryptocurrency.
PDF file concept
A PDF file is a common document format used to share text, images, and forms while preserving layout.
also: PDF
Pentagon organization
The Pentagon is the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense and is often used to refer to that department.
people_with_link concept
people_with_link is a sharing setting meaning anyone with the link may be able to access a file or document.
Per-tool prompts concept
Per-tool prompts are separate AI instructions customized for each tool an AI agent can use.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
personal data concept
Information relating to an identifiable individual, such as name, email, location, or financial details.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
Phish concept
Phish is a label for a deceptive message designed to trick a recipient.
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
phishing email technique
A phishing email is a fake or deceptive message designed to trick someone into revealing information or clicking something harmful.
phishing kit tool
A pre-packaged set of tools and templates that allows even non-technical criminals to launch phishing campaigns easily.
phishing-as-a-service concept
Phishing-as-a-service is a criminal service that sells ready-made tools and infrastructure for running phishing attacks.
phone numbers concept
Phone numbers are the unique numbers used to reach people or devices on telephone networks.
photographs concept
Photographs are images that can contain sensitive visual details or hidden metadata such as time and location.
PHP file concept
A PHP file is a web server script file written in the PHP programming language.

PHP File Creation in WordPress Plugin Directory means a PHP file was written into a WordPress plugin folder, which can be suspicious if attackers are trying to install a web shell.
php-fpm product
php-fpm is software that runs PHP code for web servers, commonly used to power PHP-based websites.
physical security concept
Physical security protects buildings, equipment, and people from real-world access, theft, or damage.
physical threats concept
Physical threats are dangers involving real-world harm to people, buildings, devices, or other tangible assets.
Picus whitepaper other
A Picus whitepaper is a security research or guidance document published by or associated with Picus.
